scope: Simulated reference software; host/kernel/admin trusted. No human risk acceptance or product certification.

threats.abuse: Compromised control replaces protection endpoint or UI reaches administration
threats.controls: Distinct writable producer volumes, immutable aliases, read-only clients; no admin mounts
threats.residual: Native same-UID and trusted host can bypass mount boundaries; a compromised producer can lie about its own telemetry.

threats.abuse: Abrupt broker/supervisor death leaves orphan computation or implies safe outputs
threats.controls: Linux parent-death signal with PID recheck; plant watchdog; incomplete-run recovery
threats.residual: Cleanup is not observed actuator state; kernel/host loss and forced death can prevent final manifest/log completion.

threats.controls: Fixed frame/depth/number/worker limits and deadlines; terminal plant arbitration
threats.residual: Authorized or local hostile traffic can deny service or force a protective stop. These local endpoints do not promise uninterrupted availability.

threats.abuse: Forged admin commands, stale revision/replay, modified evidence or secret export
threats.controls: Per-incarnation random filesystem credential, epoch-bound revision, immutable run config, hashes and explicit exports
threats.residual: Hashes detect accidental/tampered inconsistencies, not a malicious trusted administrator recomputing all metadata; no remote authentication service.

threats.abuse: Changed archive, floating image/action, unknown license or vulnerable package
threats.controls: Pinned TLS/SHA sources, reviewed selected profile/notices, actual inventories and SBOM
threats.residual: Root/image/system packages have separate obligations; database non-matches are not assurance of coverage or absence of vulnerabilities.

threats.abuse: Private standards/secrets enter context, artifact or privileged PR workflow
threats.controls: Explicit context/publication allowlists, no recursive upload, read-only contents and no stored checkout token
threats.residual: Trusted maintainer/workflow compromise and hosted runner infrastructure remain outside container isolation; logs expire under repository retention.

threats.asset_boundary: Shared plant, runner, clock and host
threats.abuse: Common algorithm/configuration/kernel/resource failure defeats both decisions
threats.controls: Separate processes/role observations/direct arbitration; bounded errors/watchdog and sanitizer/fault tests
threats.residual: Simulation/container separation does not establish independent hardware; shared plant, broker/admin, clock, physical sensors and host remain common causes.
